summary: @servicetitan/dte-unlayer preinstall runs obfuscated 727KB payload under downloaded Bun runtime
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases at install time, extracts it to a temp directory, and uses that freshly-fetched alternate runtime to execute a bundled sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, 'math_init.js')])`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line, heavily-obfuscated file with hex-named identifiers, a string-array shuffle routine (`WV8StW`), a large mixed numeric/string constant table, and decoder alphabets — its contents do not map to the package's advertised purpose (a ServiceTitan wrapper around the Unlayer email editor). Fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundled script is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the executed code path is not analyzed by Node-focused install-time scanners. Additionally, `math_init.js` and `setup.mjs` sit at the tarball root but are not covered by the declared `"files": ["dist", "src"]` allowlist, consistent with content injected outside the author's declared publish surface. Installing the package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
